2. Respondents 1 to 4 filed the aforesaid Miscellaneous case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Pabna, praying for pre-emption of the case land. 

 5. It was also stated in the petition that pre-emptors are co-sharers and contiguous land owners of 'Ka' schedule land but they were not co-sharers or contiguous owners of `Kha' and `Ga' schedule lands. 

 11. Mr. Shamsul Hoque Chowdhury, the learned Counsel, appearing for some of the respondents, however, argues that the learned Judge of the High Court Division in revision under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure rightly refused to interfere with the finding of fact arrived at by the lower appellate Court, as regards the co-share ship and contiguous ownership of the pre-emptors. He further argues that Exts. C and C (1) relates to recording of separate khatian and jama under the Bengal Tenancy Act in the name of Azizur Rahman and the said exhibits are, therefore, not proof of separation of jama under section 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the lower appellate Court correctly held that there was no legal evidence about splitting up of the holding. 

 12. The trial Court held that the appellants (0.P. in the trial Court) filed C.S. Khatian No.144 being the original khatian and C.S. Khatian No. 144/2 and hal khatian 291, Exts. C and C (1) respectively showing recording of a separate khatian and separate jote and jama under B.T. Act in the name of Azizur Rahman creating separate jama. It was further held that Dakhilas Ext. B series also support the contention that jama of Azizur Rahman was separated from his time and rent was paid exclusively by him for his purchased portion. The aforesaid khatians were prepared before the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force, by an order passed by a competent revenue officer and the order was given effect to by the co-sharers of the holding who paid rents and as such the holding stood separated under the law. So even if the order was not passed under section 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act such order cannot be overlooked in deciding a pre-emption petition under section 96 of the said Act. The pre-emptors prayed for pre-emption in 3 schedules Ka, Kha and Ga out of which admittedly they were not co-sharers as regards Kha and Ga schedules. On the basis of Exts. C and C (1) the trial Court found that the pre-emptors were not co-sharers to Ka schedule land.
